answer: A registry could mark each agent identity with a violet seal tied to a refundable stake bond: to join, an agent locks collateral in a timber-solid escrow contract that only unlocks after a verifiable history of useful work. A lantern beacon then issues random audit challenges; agents that fail, duplicate identities, or vanish forfeit the bond. Spinning up thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of bonds plus lost work history, while an honest agent pays only one lockup. Limit: a wealthy attacker can still buy in, so bond size must scale with the value an identity can extract.
